title: Information Technology Risk and Governance Disclosures: Are JSE-Listed Companies Ready for King V?
content: King V, published on 31 October 2025, applies to financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2026 and substantially revises the technology and risk governance requirements of King IV. This study assesses the readiness of the 100 largest JSE-listed companies for these requirements before King V takes effect. Using content analysis, the 2025 financial year reports of 98 companies were coded against a 35-item King V readiness checklist covering risk governance, data and information governance, technology governance, and oversight and transition. Each item was classified as carried forward, extended or new relative to King IV. Coding reliability was tested by two independent coders on 31% of the sample. Mean readiness was 59.7%; 68 companies scored between 50% and 79%, and no company met all requirements in full. Readiness fell from 66.6% on carried-forward requirements to 57.5% on extended and 38.5% on new requirements, a gradient observed in 90 of the 98 companies. Risk governance was strongest (77.1%), while data, technology, and oversight and transition governance were close to 54%. Artificial intelligence was described more often than governed, and only 11.2% of companies fully disclosed their plans for the transition to King V. This is the first assessment of readiness for King V. It shifts governance disclosure research from retrospective compliance to forward-looking readiness, and contributes a reusable readiness instrument and a pre-implementation baseline against which compliance under King V can be measured.
